references.text: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and God saw that Leah was unloved. This is an example of a man with two wives where one is loved and the other is unloved.
Leah bore sons to Jacob while she was the unloved wife, reflecting the situation described in Deuteronomy regarding the firstborn son of the unloved wife.
The rivalry between Rachel and Leah illustrates the dynamics between a loved and a less-loved wife in a polygamous marriage.
Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. He loved Hannah, but Peninnah had children. This shows a similar situation with two wives and unequal love.
Sarah demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away in favor of Isaac, even though Ishmael was the firstborn. God's law in Deuteronomy protects the firstborn from such injustice.
Isaac loved Esau while Rebekah loved Jacob. The parents' favoritism toward their children is a theme that the law in Deuteronomy seeks to regulate.
